question: Linezolid reached patients in 2000 and daptomycin in 2003, each the first of a new class. When were their families first found?
answer: In the 1980s, then set aside. DuPont announced the oxazolidinones in 1987 before dropping them; Upjohn chemists later refined the family into linezolid. Eli Lilly found daptomycin in the early 1980s and halted trials in 1991 over muscle toxicity; Cubist licensed it in 1997. The new classes of the 2000s were old shelf stock.
move: A launch date says when a thing arrived, not when it began.
trap: Assuming a drug was discovered shortly before the year it was approved.
source: Eisenstein, Oleson & Baltz, Clinical Infectious Diseases, 2010
